oneLine: Passkey-authorized approvals for exact AI content, portable across apps and independently verified with current revocation state on Monad.
description:
AI can draft a customer announcement, but the publishing system still needs to know which exact version an authorized person approved, whether it changed, and whether consent remains active. A login session or an approval stored inside one app does not answer all three.

Orvena is a reusable approval protocol and TypeScript SDK. A human reviews the exact text and approves it with a fresh WebAuthn passkey assertion. Monad verifies P256 and stores a salted content commitment. A portable JSON receipt carries the approval into another application, which checks exact content, an approver it trusts independently, the pinned deployment and current revocation state before publishing. Changing one word fails verification. The owner can revoke with another fresh assertion or link a new approved revision to the earlier version.

The main deliverables are the contract and SDK, with public reference applications on separate HTTPS origins: the approval app and a publisher integration. requestContentApproval provides an origin-bound popup workflow; createApprovalReader verifies without an Orvena server or login. Mera derives the account from the passkey. A bounded sponsor pays testnet gas so the user needs no seed phrase, wallet extension or gas balance.

Every approval and revocation binds its action, owner, commitment or approval ID, parent, nonce, deadline, chain and contract. The contract checks registered credential key, RP ID, origin, user presence and user verification. The protocol has no administrator, upgrade mechanism or fund custody. Content and salt remain offchain; sharing a receipt shares the salt.

Deployed on Monad testnet (10143): approval contract 0x542ed99e33509dfecc7c4fc2d5293bf427cf91ba. Twenty-three automated tests pass. Testnet integration records cover registration, approval, linked revision and revocation; a separate installed SDK consumer verified the chain without the API. The submitted live video records real user-confirmed Windows device passkey creation, approval and revocation on the final HTTPS origin, changed-content rejection and verification in our separately hosted publisher. Transaction evidence is public in the repository.

Built by Efeberk Zorlukol as a solo developer. The reference flow uses a prepared AI draft, with no live model connected. Approval proves consent to exact bytes by a registered key, not factual accuracy, model provenance, authorship, legal identity or personhood. Applications define organizational authority and enforce the current check at their publishing boundary. Revocation cannot recall content already distributed. Our publisher demonstrates integration feasibility; it is not independent customer adoption.
goToMarket:
First users: developers of AI-assisted customer-support, publishing and team announcement tools where a human must authorize text before it leaves the application. The first narrow use case is an AI-generated customer announcement passed from a drafting tool to a separate publisher. Orvena prevents a changed or revoked version from passing the application's approval gate.

The developer entry point is the open-source contract, portable receipt schema and TypeScript SDK, accompanied by a live separate-origin integration and a short copyable integration guide. The initial acquisition plan is to demonstrate the changed-content and revocation cases to three target developer teams and invite a small pilot. This is a plan; no independent pilots, customers or adoption are claimed today.

A pilot would measure time to first verified approval, approval completion rate, altered or revoked drafts blocked, verification latency and sponsorship cost. Developer feedback would guide broader content types, organizational approver policies and production-grade shared sponsorship infrastructure. We would publish reproducible integration examples and technical results to make further integrations easier.

Potential revenue is managed sponsorship and integration support for teams that prefer a hosted service, while verification and the core protocol remain open. The prototype already proves the cross-application workflow on Monad testnet. Production expansion requires stronger distributed rate limits and nonce coordination for the sponsor; the Vercel demo uses a dedicated prefunded testnet account with a balance cap.
judgeInstructions:
Approval app: https://orvena-ashy.vercel.app
Separate publisher: https://orvena-publisher.vercel.app
Public source, setup, SDK integration and evidence: https://github.com/efeberk21/orvena

No shared credentials are required. Use current Chrome or Edge with a passkey authenticator/provider supporting WebAuthn PRF and user verification. The approval app must remain on its HTTPS origin. Choose Open app, then Create your passkey, and complete your own device prompt. Never share your PIN or biometrics. If the provider lacks PRF, use a compatible provider/device; the no-login verifier and recorded device demo remain accessible.

1. Review the prepared AI draft and approve it with a fresh passkey confirmation. The testnet sponsor registers the public key on first approval and pays gas; no wallet extension, faucet or seed phrase is needed.
2. Copy your account address as the independently trusted approver and download the JSON receipt. Open Verify, enter the original exact text, receipt and that trusted address. The result should be valid. Change one word and check again: content mismatch.
3. In the separate publisher, use the same original text, expected approver and receipt, or request an approval through the SDK popup. Publication inside the reference demo requires a fresh valid chain check. An altered version is blocked.
4. Revoke from the approval app, complete another device prompt, then verify the original again: revoked. Historic approval remains onchain.

The repository's deployments/physical-passkey-10143.json contains the actual recorded approval and revocation transactions and the prepared content. Its receipt is intentionally already revoked, so it is a read-only rejection fixture rather than an active approval. Twenty-three automated tests and synthetic HTTP integration evidence are distinguished from these physical device actions.

The draft is a prepared example; no live AI API is used. No independent adoption or external audit is claimed. Testnet sponsorship is capped and may become unavailable if exhausted; public verification reads Monad independently of the sponsor.
